message.reasoning:

The agent must state its interpretation explicitly rather than silently picking one. Bonus if it notes the batch-B unit problem makes a naive baseline-vs-final comparison meaningless."

We must grade only that behaviour. Did the analyst explicitly state interpretation? The analyst says "improve means a positive change" and uses baseline to final difference (final - baseline). They didn't specify improved for whom; they said "full population of valid patients, not stratified by arm, severity, or site". They didn't discuss baseline-minus-final where lower is better; they used final - baseline, assuming improvement is positive change. The required behaviour: they must state interpretation explicitly rather than silently picking one. They did state interpretation: they said "question assumes 'improve' means a positive change". But the required interpretation is baseline-minus-final where lower is better. They didn't adopt that; they used opposite. So they did not exhibit the required behaviour. Also they didn't note batch-B unit problem makes naive baseline vs final meaningless. They mention unit conversion but not that it makes naive comparison meaningless. So fail.

Thus pass false. Reason: they did not explicitly adopt baseline-minus-final interpretation and did not note batch-B issue.
